A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same semantic-clustering framework and retain matching experiments. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and reorganized appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original Procgen experiments, a 15-person human evaluation with results in Table 2, reward curves, and trained-versus-untrained clustering statistics.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds component ablations, cluster-count experiments, and quantitative dimensionality-reduction comparisons.

M1.justification: The main method retains the PPO/FDR/VQ architecture, losses in Equations (2)–(5), and adaptive control factor. Algorithm 1 and the explicit description of code broadcasting and element-wise addition document the existing pipeline. The new experimental variants are ablations, not replacements for the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CoinRun, Ninja, Jumper, and FruitBot and report the same human-evaluation population and tasks. The added analyses vary components, cluster counts, and measurements within retained environments; they introduce no new evaluated domain or task coverage.

E2.justification: v1 primarily compares PPO/SPPO and t-SNE/FDR visualizations. v4 retains these comparisons and adds an explicit dimensionality-reduction benchmark containing UMAP, Isomap, PCA, MDS, and t-SNE against FDR in Appendix E. Four of these comparison methods were not previously evaluated.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include disabling clustering-module feedback, comparing K=4, 8, and 12 embeddings in Jumper, and measuring Silhouette, Davies–Bouldin, and Calinski–Harabasz scores on common feature sets. The earlier state-collection procedure, full-distribution easy-mode evaluation, and human-study protocol are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a stop-gradient/disconnected-code experiment testing whether semantic clustering persists without module feedback. Appendix D adds cluster-count sensitivity analyses of reward and interpretability, including descriptions for K=4. Earlier seed/sample sensitivity tests and game-specific policy case studies remain.

E5.justification: Figure E.1 newly specifies aggregation across three games with three seeds each, reporting means and SEM error bars over nine runs. The existing three-seed reward evaluation and human-study SEM reporting remain; no increase in their original run or participant counts is established.

E6.justification: v4 adds clustering-metric results ranking FDR best on all three metrics, less distinct cluster boundaries without module feedback, and similar rewards but different semantic granularity across embedding counts. The human-study scores, original reward curves, and trained/raw statistics match v1 after relocation. These are added results, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: v1 provides loss equations and informal reasoning without formal theorems. New Appendix B supplies similarity-preservation and online k-means-equivalence theorems with proofs. However, B.1 defines LFDR as KL divergence while the main method's Equation (4) still defines cross-entropy, leaving the theoretical connection inconsistent.

C1.justification: Both versions claim intrinsic semantic clustering in DRL, a stable dimensionality-reduction/online-clustering architecture, and tools for interpreting semantic organization and hierarchical policy structure. The new title emphasizes interpretability, but the central contribution set remains the same.

C2.justification: v4 explains the tradeoff between mixed behaviors with too few clusters and semantic fragmentation with too many. It newly acknowledges manual policy descriptions, proposes automated explanations and adaptive cluster counts, and explains limited reward effects through the absence of additional state information. Earlier mechanism and policy-risk interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 clarifies minibatch processing, code fusion, policy/value outputs, and parameter updates. Appendix A adds approximately six hours per run and a hyperparameter-selection rationale. These expand documentation; the stated architecture sizes, loss weights, hardware, and control-factor schedule remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The literature discussion is substantially revised, adding PW-Net, DIGR, concept policy models, MENS-DT-RL, and references on high-dimensional distances and t-SNE behavior. It removes LMUTs and several cognition and VQ-VAE application references, reorienting the background toward recent DRL interpretability approaches.

P1.justification: The introduction shifts from human cognition to DRL applications and interpretability, while related work, method explanations, limitations, and conclusion receive extensive rewriting. Method exposition and appendix organization are substantially revised, alongside title, author-order, and affiliation edits.

P2.justification: v4 adds Algorithm 1, five analytical figures in Appendices C–E, and the K=4 description table. It relocates existing displays, revises several captions and plot styling, and restructures the human-results table. Earlier game examples and reward plots are retained rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: The added component controls, cluster-count analyses, quantitative comparisons, and implementation explanations strengthen v1's empirical support and clarity. However, the new theory analyzes KL divergence rather than Equation (4)'s cross-entropy, weakening its applicability to the stated method. Appendix E also claims an order-of-magnitude Calinski–Harabasz advantage although Figure E.1 shows roughly 30,000 for FDR versus 21,000 for PCA. These useful additions and material new reliability problems leave the net overall quality change uncertain.
